tagline: Mountains, megacities, and global pop culture
overview:
South Korea occupies the southern half of the Korean Peninsula in East Asia, surrounded by sea on three sides and separated from North Korea by a fortified border in the north. It covers about 100,000 km², a little larger than Indiana, and mountains take up around 70 percent of that.

About 52 million people live in South Korea, speaking Korean and writing with hangul, an alphabet designed in the 1440s to be easy to learn. Seoul, the capital, sits on the Han River, and its metropolitan area holds roughly half the country's population, making it one of the largest urban regions on Earth.

South Korea is a democratic republic with an elected president. In a single lifetime it went from one of the world's poorest countries to a technology powerhouse making phones, ships, cars and semiconductors, while its music, films and television have found huge audiences worldwide.
landAndNature: Mountain ridges run down the east coast, dropping steeply to the sea, while the west and south flatten into rice plains and thousands of small islands. Jeju, a volcanic island in the south, has the country's highest peak, Hallasan at 1,947 meters, plus lava tube caves and stone walls built against the wind. The four seasons are distinct: cold, dry winters, a rainy season in summer called jangma, and autumn foliage that draws crowds to the mountains. Tidal flats along the west coast, where the tide can retreat kilometers, feed millions of migrating shorebirds. Asiatic black bears have been reintroduced to Jirisan, and the Demilitarized Zone, empty of people since 1953, shelters cranes and other rare wildlife.
peopleAndCulture: Korean meals arrive with banchan, many small side dishes, around rice and soup; kimchi, cabbage fermented with chili and garlic, is at almost every table, and families once buried jars of it to ferment through winter. Korean barbecue is grilled at the table, and bibimbap mixes rice with vegetables and egg. K-pop groups fill stadiums worldwide, and the film Parasite won the Academy Award for best picture in 2020, the first in a language other than English. Taekwondo, a Korean martial art, is an Olympic sport, and baseball and soccer draw big crowds. Competitive video gaming is a professional career with televised leagues. Chuseok, the autumn harvest festival, sends millions traveling home to honor ancestors.
history: Korean kingdoms, Goguryeo, Baekje and Silla, competed for the peninsula 1,500 years ago before Silla unified it. The Goryeo dynasty gave Korea its English name and printed books with movable metal type decades before Gutenberg. The Joseon dynasty ruled from 1392 to 1910; King Sejong's scholars created the hangul alphabet in 1443 so ordinary people could read. Japan annexed Korea in 1910 and ruled harshly until 1945. At the end of World War II the peninsula was divided at the 38th parallel, Soviet forces in the north and American in the south, and two rival states formed in 1948. The Korean War of 1950–1953 killed millions and ended in an armistice, leaving the division in place. South Korea grew rapidly under military rulers, then became a full democracy after mass protests in 1987.
funFacts: The hangul alphabet was invented in the 1440s with letter shapes that copy the position of the mouth and tongue.
South Korea has some of the fastest internet in the world, and professional video gamers are treated as sports stars.
Koreans traditionally counted themselves a year old at birth, so many people had two different ages until the rules changed in 2023.
On Jeju island, haenyeo women have dived for shellfish without air tanks for centuries, some still working past age seventy.
Seoul's subway has hundreds of stations, mobile phone signal in every tunnel, and heated seats in winter.
